thread:
olivia (support): Customer ACME-prod on Dedicated Private reported sudden 401s starting after we migrated their VPC to go through the new NAT-LB this morning. They say requests succeed if they hit the service via internal IP, but fail when routed through the LB. Logs show 'missing api_key' from our auth layer. Need help triaging — they block production traffic.

kevin (eng-infra): ok thanks. quick q: are they sending API keys in Authorization header (Bearer) or custom header?

olivia (support): they're sending standard Authorization: Bearer <redwood-api-key> in the request to https://acme-private.redwood.internal/v1/generate. curl from their side (example they sent):

olivia (support): ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live:ACME123" \   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \   https://acme-private.redwood.internal/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

maria (eng-platform): when you curl the internal IP directly (bypassing LB) do you see the Authorization header reach the service? can you paste `curl -I` or a tcpdump?

olivia (support): they ran these:

olivia (support): ```
# from app pod -> service IP (works)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live:ACME123" http://10.32.45.12:8080/health -v
# shows header in service logs: Authorization: Bearer sk_live:ACME123

# from external -> LB -> service (fails)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live:ACME123" https://acme-private.redwood.internal/v1/generate -v
# service logs show no Authorization header, auth layer returns 401 missing api_key
```

kevin (eng-infra): that points to LB / proxy stripping Authorization. New NAT-LB we configured sits in front and does TLS terminate + proxy. By default some proxies remove or normalize Authorization for security. Which LB type? internal-GCP-NAT or an APIGateway?

olivia (support): internal GCP TCP LB with an internal HTTP(S) proxy (we converted to use managed proxy recently).

kevin (eng-infra): known behavior: GCP HTTP(S) proxy will remove certain headers unless allowed. For K8s + Istio we also saw Envoy filters that drop auth headers when header_key matches. First repro step for us: curl LB with `-H "Authorization: foo" -v` and run `tcpdump -i any port 8080 -A` on the backend pod to see what arrives. If Authorization missing, it's LB.

maria (eng-platform): also check ingress / envoy config. If using Istio IngressGateway, there is an EnvoyFilter that may apply header sanitizer. Search for filters that match `authorization`/`x-google-*`.

kevin (eng-infra): quick workaround for customer: add a second header that we accept, e.g., X-Forwarded-Authorization, while we fix LB. But long-term we prefer passing the standard Authorization.

sre-oncall: FYI I hit a similar issue last quarter when Nginx ingress had `proxy_hide_header Authorization;` in a custom snippet. Two fixes: (1) configure the proxy to forward Authorization: `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` or (2) add EnvoyFilter to preserve header in Istio: set `request_headers_to_add` or remove header removal in `remove_headers`.

olivia (support): customer tried adding API key in query param ?api_key=... as a stopgap and that worked. They don't want to do that for security.

kevin (eng-infra): proposed plan: 1) reproduce and confirm header is stripped at LB 2) open infra change to add passthrough/preserve Authorization 3) add temporary per-customer rule to accept X-Forwarded-Authorization for their VPC 4) schedule patch for all private LB configs to preserve Authorization for Redwood-managed services.

maria (eng-platform): for Istio customers, here's an EnvoyFilter snippet we can apply quickly (replace namespaced values):

maria (eng-platform): ```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: preserve-authorization-header
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      istio: ingressgateway
  configPatches:
    - applyTo: NETWORK_FILTER
      match:
        listener:
          filterChain:
            filter:
              name: "envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager"
      patch:
        operation: MERGE
        value:
          typed_config:
            '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.network.http_connection_manager.v3.HttpConnectionManager
            request_headers_to_add:
              - header:
                  key: "authorization"
                  value: "%REQ(authorization)%"
                append_action: OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD
```

maria (eng-platform): that forces the gateway to copy the incoming header into the request. Use with care.

kevin (eng-infra): for GCP HTTP(S) proxy specifically, doc says to set `preserve_host` and configure `backendConfig` to pass certain headers, or use the `enable-cdn` false and add `customRequestHeaders`. I'll open a change.

olivia (support): I ran tcpdump with the customer and confirmed Authorization present at the client -> LB connection, but missing on backend -> service. So LB/proxy is removing it. sending their tcpdump output to the thread: `client->lb: Authorization: Bearer sk_live:ACME123` then `lb->backend: (no authorization header)`.

sre-oncall: tagging this as P1 since it's a production auth-blocker for a customer. assigning infra.

kevin (eng-infra): creating ticket INFRA-2338, draft change to add `customRequestHeaders` to the backend service for the customer's LB and to roll out EnvoyFilter for Istio-ingress in staging first. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-2338

kevin (eng-infra): temporary patch applied to their per-customer LB (customRequestHeaders: X-Forwarded-Authorization: $http_authorization). Customer verified and now reports success, no 401s.

olivia (support): customer confirms: :tada: production traffic restored. They want a permanent fix across all Private clusters.

maria (eng-platform): action items:
- (kevin) roll out LB config change to preserve Authorization in the GCP HTTP(S) proxy for private deployments.
- (maria) add an automated test in dedicated e2e that verifies Authorization header survives the full path (client -> LB -> ingress -> service).
- (platform) draft a KB article: "Auth header missing after NAT/LB migration" with repro steps + temporary mitigation (X-Forwarded-Authorization) + Istio EnvoyFilter snippet.

kevin (eng-infra): will schedule change in next infra maintenance window; will do canary to two customers first.

kevin (eng-infra): agreed — adding tf-lint rule to INFRA-2338.
